name: v0.3.10 fresh transfer
one_shot_semantics: Run the preregistered matrix once after protocol commit and fresh-target freeze commit. Rerun only exact cells that fail for infrastructure reasons. Do not change budgets, policies, seeds, or the app after seeing outcomes.
research_question: Does the frozen v0.3.9 return-cycle guard transfer to a fresh application shape without introducing false escapes or return regressions?
success_means: Protocol integrity and reproducible evidence, not necessarily Outcome A.

candidate.cycle_rule: During an unresolved return phase, arriving at an exact destination signature already seen in that phase (parent not matched) is a return cycle. First exact repeat triggers escape. No N, no cluster-only trigger, no app hardcode.
candidate.escape_semantics: Abandon active branch: returning=false, active_branch empty, parent cleared, commitment_left=0. Do not _complete_branch. Do not increment return_success / completed_total. Do not add to returned/completed. Event return_cycle_escape; optional sequence_terminal outcome return_cycle_abandoned if instance still open.

fresh_target.name: buggy-desk
fresh_target.description: Deterministic internal support/service-desk Web benchmark, distinct from BuggyShop and BuggyFlow.

matrix.seed_rationale: All matrix policies are deterministic (GhostPolicy without LLM, BFS, DFS). No RandomPolicy/Monkey. Single seed is seed-invariant.

c1_cycle_detector.rule: An evaluable return-cycle opportunity exists when an unresolved return phase revisits the same exact destination signature before matching the recorded parent.
c1_cycle_detector.consistency: For guard, every escape should correspond to such an opportunity.

S3.name: same cluster, distinct exact variants
S3.expected: zero escape solely because cluster repeats/similarity occurs

S4.name: exact self-loop
S4.expected: exactly one escape, abandoned, not returned

S5.name: short A→B→A cycle
S5.expected: escape on first exact repeated destination, branch abandoned, no return success

S6.name: history reset between branches
S6.expected: cycle history from branch one must not poison branch two

S7.name: finding then cycle
S7.expected: finding followed by cycle escape must not convert into successful return

contamination.buggy_shop: excluded from this round; historical inspected case only
contamination.deepbench: historical regression only, not a tuning or generalization target
contamination.fresh_target_results: must not be used to change candidate behavior in this round

A.label: fresh transfer with safety
all: Fresh target contains at least one evaluable return-cycle opportunity under primary budget 120.
Guard emits at least one valid return_cycle_escape on fresh target.
At least one escape is followed by novel state or novel URL absent from corresponding C1 evidence.
Guard @120 loses no C1 confirmed bug.
S4/S5 produce expected abandonment and zero successful-return inflation.
Historical DeepBench/v0.3.9 regression evidence still verifies.
A.interpretation: one fresh application transfer under a frozen candidate

B.label: safe but no demonstrated transfer benefit
B.when: Safety passes, no C1 bug loss, but no fresh escape, or escape produces no measurable post-escape novelty, or guard/C1 are effectively equivalent.

C.label: harmful/regression
any: guard loses any C1 confirmed bug @120
historical freeze/regression invariant fails because of this round

D.label: inconclusive target
D.when: Fresh target never produces an evaluable return-cycle opportunity under preregistered budget while safety otherwise passes.
D.stop: Do not raise budget or redesign app after seeing D.

authoring_bias_disclosure_required: BuggyDesk was authored after v0.3.9 existed.
v0.3.9 candidate was frozen before target evaluation.
BuggyDesk was frozen before policy evaluation.
This is a fresh one-target cross-app transfer test, not an independently designed external benchmark and not universal generalization proof.
